name: Italian Game
family: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Italian Game (Giuoco Piano, Evans Gambit, Two Knights Defence)
summary: The Italian Game (1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4) puts the bishop on its most aggressive square, aiming at f7, the weakest point in Black's camp. This repertoire plays it in the open, classical way: against 3...Bc5 we build the c3+d4 centre (Giuoco Piano, 7.Bd2 main line, with the Moller Attack and the Evans Gambit as sharper options), and against 3...Nf6 we attack f7 at once with 4.Ng5, which sets up the Fried Liver and Lolli attacks if Black recaptures on d5. A quiet Giuoco Pianissimo setup with d3 is included as an alternative repertoire, plus clear answers and traps against every other third move.
keyIdeas: f7 is the target: Bc4 plus Ng5 or Qf3/Qb3/Qh5 pressure is the theme in almost every line.
Against 3...Bc5 build the centre with c3 and d4; after ...exd4 cxd4 the c5-bishop must leave with ...Bb4+.
In the 7.Bd2 main line White gets an isolated d4-pawn: keep pieces active (Qb3, Rfe1, Ne4/Ne5) so it is a strength, not a weakness.
Against 3...Nf6 play 4.Ng5: 5...Nxd5?! allows the Fried Liver (6.Nxf7!) or the Lolli (6.d4); 5...Na5 costs Black a pawn for activity.
When the opponent wastes time (3...h6, 3...g6, 3...Be7, 3...d6) open the centre with d4.
In the quiet d3 setups the standard plan is O-O, Re1, Bb3, h3 and the Nbd2-f1-g3 knight manoeuvre, with d4 at the right moment.
Know the traps on both sides: Legal's mate and the Fried Liver for you; the Blackburne Shilling (4.Nxe5? Qg5!) and the Traxler (5.Nxf7?! Bxf2+) against you.
typicalPlans: Giuoco Piano 5.d4: after the bishop trade on d2, play Qb3, O-O, Rfe1, then Ne4/Ne5 and Bd3 with kingside pressure around the isolated d4-pawn.
Two Knights 5...Na5: keep the extra pawn with Bb5+, Be2, Nf3-e5, then d4, b3, Bb2, Nd2 and castle; trade pieces to reach an endgame a pawn up.
Fried Liver: after 6.Nxf7 Kxf7 7.Qf3+ Ke6 8.Nc3 Nb4 castle and open the centre with d4; the king in the middle is worth more than the piece.
Evans Gambit: c3 and d4 with tempo, castle, Ba3 to stop Black from castling, and fast rook activity on the open central files.
Giuoco Pianissimo: Re1, Bb3 (or Bc2), h3, Nbd2-f1-g3, then d4 or Nh4-f5 depending on what Black does.
commonMistakes: Grabbing e5 against the Blackburne Shilling Gambit: 3...Nd4 4.Nxe5? Qg5! wins material and 5.Nxf7?? even loses to mate.
Answering the Traxler (4.Ng5 Bc5) with the greedy 5.Nxf7; 5.Bxf7+! is safe and strong.
In the Fried Liver, playing the old 9.a3?! (9...Nxc2+! is good for Black) instead of 9.O-O.
In the 6.cxd4 Bb4+ line, playing 7.Bd2 and then allowing ...Nxe4 without knowing the Bxf7+ and Qb3+ fork that wins the material back.
Playing h3 or a3 automatically instead of developing: the Italian is about speed and central control.
Letting the isolated d4-pawn become passive: in IQP positions keep pieces active and avoid trading into a bad endgame.

lines.name: Giuoco Piano: 4.c3 Nf6 5.d4 exd4 6.cxd4 Bb4+ 7.Bd2 (main line)
lines.description: The classical main line and our recommended answer to 3...Bc5: build the c3+d4 centre, block the check with 7.Bd2 and after the trade on d2 play the isolated-queen's-pawn middlegame with active pieces (Qb3, Rfe1, Ne4/Ne5). 10...Na5 11.Qa4+ Nc6 12.Qb3 is a known way for Black to force a repetition.
lines.evaluation: Equal to slightly better for White (+0.2): more space and activity versus the isolated d4-pawn.

lines.name: Giuoco Piano: 7.Bd2 Nxe4 (Kaufman simplification)

lines.evaluation: Equal (0.0): queens come off early; play for small endgame pressure.

lines.name: Giuoco Piano: Moller Attack 7.Nc3 Nxe4 8.O-O Bxc3 9.d5
lines.description: The romantic alternative to 7.Bd2: White gambits the e4-pawn for development and attacks along the e-file. The main line ends in a perpetual check after the Nxh7 sacrifice. lines.name: Giuoco Piano: 4.c3 Qe7 (Closed Variation)
lines.description: Black protects e5 in advance so the centre stays closed. White simply takes space: d4, castles, a4 to chase the b6-bishop, then d5 and c4 with a big queenside space advantage. Other replies: 5...exd4 6.O-O! d3 7.e5 is very strong for White (+1.3); 6...Nf6 7.b4 or 7.a4 follows the same space-gaining plan; 6...a6 7.dxe5 Nxe5 8.Nxe5 Qxe5 9.Nd2 wins time on the queen. 4...Bb6 5.d4 Qe7 transposes here; 4...Qf6 is met by 5.b4 or 5.a4 (gaining queenside space with tempo on the bishop), then d3 and Na3.
lines.evaluation: White is clearly better (+1.0): more space and an easy queenside plan.
